title: Club Membership: how the medical-hold waiver amount is finalized
content:
## Scope
This document states, for Club Membership, how the outstanding balance available to waive and the employer-funded share of it combine into the club's own posted medical-hold dues waiver amount.

## Rule
The club's own waiver amount is the outstanding balance available to waive, less the employer-funded share of it, rounded to 2 decimal places only at the end of the calculation, with no intermediate rounding. The club's own waiver amount is never posted as a negative figure.

## Worked example (hypothetical)
Suppose the outstanding balance available to waive is $120.00, and the employer-funded share, once computed, comes to $30.00. The club's own waiver amount is $120.00 less $30.00, giving $90.00.

## Points of judgement
Where no employer-funded share applies at all, the club's own waiver amount is simply the full outstanding balance available to waive, rounded to 2 decimal places; where the employer-funded share happens to equal the entire outstanding balance, the club's own waiver amount is $0.00, never a negative figure.
